summary: The fleet mTLS CA private key, the parent leaf private key, and the fleet PSK previously sat in plaintext in the myseliasan control-plane database (ControlSetting rows) — anyone able to read that database could impersonate the fleet CA or the shared secret and take over every adopted node. These three values are now AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest (reusing the existing infra/atrest module, the same one mymatasan uses for recordings/snapshots/training images) whenever encryption at rest is enabled. New apps/myseliasan/services/secret_store.go adds encodeSecret/decodeSecret helpers (base64(atrest ciphertext) in the TEXT settings column); fleet_ca.go and node_registry.go route the CA/parent private keys and the fleet PSK through them. app.go adds openFleetSecretCipher, which resolves the cipher from the same shared `security` config block mymatasan already documents (encryptAtRest, keyPath, keyProtector, passphrase/passphraseFile/passphraseEnv, recoveryPath) before the node registry is built. Public certificates and the revocation list are unaffected and remain plaintext.
compatibility: Backward compatible: encryptAtRest defaults to true but a legacy plaintext CA key/parent key/fleet PSK written before this change is read back transparently (decodeSecret passes through anything that isn't atrest-wrapped ciphertext) — no migration step and no re-adoption of existing nodes is required. Existing installs with no `security` block configured get myseliasan's own default key path (<dataDir>/secret/atrest.key, independent of mymatasan's key) the first time they boot with this change. If a key that previously existed here goes missing (moved/reimaged host, deleted key file) the app now fails closed at startup with an error rather than silently minting a new key and orphaning the encrypted CA key/PSK, which would otherwise reset the whole fleet's trust and force every node to be re-adopted; restore the key file or set security.recoveryPath and restart.
